description: Vitals Nominal turns complex crew health data into clear, at-a-glance insight, so astronauts can stay focused on the mission.
summary: On long missions to the Moon and Mars, astronauts must spot changes in their own health, often while busy, tired or far from help. VEGA is a calm health companion built into a single curved arm band. It reaches the astronaut in three ways: a flexible wrist display, a voice assistant, and a gentle haptic pulse, and it keeps flight surgeons on Earth informed through a delayed data link. Instead of showing every number, VEGA picks the three values that matter most right now and becomes simpler, not louder, when something goes wrong. Our goal is to help astronauts assess and act on their health without adding stress to an already demanding mission.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

VEGA gathers health indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep, mood, blood oxygen and exercise) and helps astronauts understand and act on them through one device, the VEGA band:

- Curved arm display: a flexible screen on the forearm. A status strip on the top edge shows the single most important message. A clickable body map shows each organ system's status, and VEGA selects the three most relevant values for the moment.

- VEGA voice assistant: astronauts can ask "Vega, how is my heart?" with their hands busy. A short morning chat logs sleep and mood without a form.

- Haptic pulse: when hands and eyes are busy, for example during a spacewalk, a gentle pulse on the wrist comes before any sound or light.

- Earth link: telemetry is sent to flight surgeons automatically, with simulated signal delay for the ISS, a Moon base and Mars transit.

HOW IT WORKS: A LOW-STRESS, ADAPTIVE INTERFACE

- Nominal: minimal information; nothing competes for attention.

- Attention: the view simplifies, VEGA explains why in a calm tone and suggests one action ("Ease your pace, you have time").

- Critical: one instruction, one focus ("Stop task, hold position"). Earth and the EVA partner are notified automatically.

Every change is announced, and the astronaut can always say "show all", so control stays with the crew. Trends and predictions help catch problems early.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- One device, focused: we deliberately dropped a helmet display so there is one place to look and nothing new inside the helmet.

- Inspired by adaptive cockpit interfaces: information is prioritized by context.

- Fit and gloves: a rigid curved display plus a stretchable strap for wrists of about 14–20 cm; voice and haptics are the main channels during spacewalks.

- Distance from Earth: on Mars, messages can take up to ~20 minutes one way, so VEGA responds first on board.

- Privacy: only the mood score is shared with Earth; voice is never recorded.

- Every indicator explains why it matters in space, how to measure it, when to tell Earth and what helps, grounded in NASA research.

IMPACT

VEGA reduces the mental load of self-monitoring, catches problems earlier and keeps astronauts calm in critical moments. The same approach could help people in other isolated, high-stress places such as polar stations, submarines or remote clinics.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Speech API, GitHub Pages, Autodesk Fusion (3D model), Procreate (sketches), Vizcom (AI-assisted renders), Claude (AI-assisted code, text, video and music).
